summary: Build GIS, route planning, vulnerability mapping, and registry skills for humanitarian delivery. Explore the practical TrainingCred course.
lede: Geospatial analysis connects location, access, vulnerability, and beneficiary data to support humanitarian assistance decisions. For humanitarian logistics and social protection professionals, this course applies that approach to delivery planning and targeting priority communities. Learners use QGIS and operational datasets to assess access, map vulnerability, calculate distribution coverage, and communicate route and targeting decisions in a logistics brief.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use location, access, vulnerability, or beneficiary data to make humanitarian delivery decisions. It supports beginner-to-intermediate GIS users who can work with spreadsheets and operational data, as well as experienced field practitioners who need a stronger bridge between mapping and logistics execution.
modules: QGIS Data Readiness and Spatial Measurement
Dynamic Beneficiary Registries and Data Governance
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in humanitarian response, social protection delivery, MEAL, emergency coordination, logistics, or GIS. Basic spreadsheet skills and the ability to interpret tables and maps are expected. No programming is required for completion. Familiarity with QGIS is useful but not essential because core spatial workflows receive guided practice. Advanced remote-sensing automation, machine-learning classification, and registry interoperability are introduced at conceptual or operational scoping level rather than production implementation level.
